item.title: Telemedicine Consultation for Pediatric Trauma in Community ED Visits and Parent Experience of Care
item.dc:creator: James P. Marcin
Jennifer L. Rosenthal
Daniel J. Tancredi
Tanya Rinderknecht
Michelle Y. Hamline
Holly Leshikar
Marike Zwienenberg
Joseph M. Galante
item.description:
Authors: James P. Marcin, Jennifer L. Rosenthal, Daniel J. Tancredi, Tanya Rinderknecht, Michelle Y. Hamline, Holly Leshikar, Marike Zwienenberg, Joseph M. Galante, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2636546
Abstract: Importance Telephone consultations for acutely injured children receiving care in emergency departments (EDs) in nonpediatric trauma centers frequently exclude direct communication and informed decision-making with parents. The use of telemedicine to facilitate real-time expert consultation and parental communication with pediatric trauma specialists is underexplored and may improve family experience and support clinical decision-making. Objective To examine the impact of telemedicine on parent experience of care, parent distress, and transfer frequency for acutely injured children presenting to EDs in nonpediatric trauma centers. Design, Setting, and Participants This stepped-wedge cluster-randomized clinical trial recruited patients between November 30, 2020, and November 27, 2022. Participants included families of children younger than 18 years with acute physical trauma presenting to 1 of 10 nonpediatric trauma centers in northern California. Analyses were conducted between June 2023 and March 2026. Interventions EDs were randomized to use telemedicine following a standard telephone consultation or the standard of care (telephone consultation only) when consulting with pediatric trauma physicians. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcomes were parent experience of care and parent distress measured 3 days or more following the child's injury. Experience of care was measured using ED Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (CAHPS) questions. Distress was measured using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory Form Y survey. Modified intention-to-treat analyses were performed to evaluate outcomes. Results The study included 595 children with acute physical trauma with a mean (SD) age of 7.6 (5.1) years, of whom 369 (62.0%) were assigned to telemedicine and 226 (38.0%) to standard of care. Summary scores for parent experience of care 3 days post injury were similar between cohorts (adjusted mean difference [AMD], 0.041 [95% CI, −0.008 to 0.090; P = .10]), as were parent distress summary scores (AMD, −0.031 [95% CI, −0.297 to 0.235; P = .82]). The adjusted odds ratio for transfer of patients assigned to telemedicine was 0.59 (95% CI, 0.16 to 2.16; P = .43). Subscale analyses found significantly higher parental ED discharge and/or transfer experience ratings for patients assigned to telemedicine (AMD, 0.104 [95% CI, 0.023 to 0.186; P = .01]). Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial, telemedicine consultations did not differ statistically significantly from standard care with respect to parent experience of care, distress, and transfer rates. Subscale analyses suggested a potential improvement with telemedicine consultations in parent experience related to ED discharge and interfacility transfers, highlighting a potential benefit in communication and preparation during care transitions. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04469036

item.title: Dual Health and Economic Burden of Multimorbidity in Aging Populations
item.dc:creator: Wenjing Ji
Jiacheng Zheng
Suzhen Guan
Yang Liu
Xi Chen
Zhuoer Lin
Joan Costa-Font
Reshma Aziz Merchant
item.description:
Authors: Wenjing Ji, Jiacheng Zheng, Suzhen Guan, Yang Liu, Xi Chen, Zhuoer Lin, Joan Costa-Font, Reshma Aziz Merchant, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2633002
Abstract: Importance Population aging is contributing to rising multimorbidity across physical, psychological, and cognitive domains, yet global evidence integrating health and economic burdens in older adults remains limited. Objectives To quantify the global health and economic burden of multimorbidity among adults aged 60 years or older and to assess trends from 2000 to 2023. Design, Setting, and Participants This economic evaluation used observational modeling of Global Burden of Disease study 2023 estimates as health inputs and integrated them with macroeconomic, health expenditure, and population data from World Bank Open Data, the World Health Organization Global Health Expenditure Database, and United Nations population data. Health burden analyses covered adults aged 60 years or older in 204 countries and territories from 2000 to 2023, and economic burden analyses covered 180 countries and territories. Data analyses were performed from January 27 to July 22, 2026. Exposures Cross-domain multimorbidity spanning physical conditions, psychological disorders, and cognitive disorders, operationalized as 78 multimorbidity combinations. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcomes were years lived with disability (YLDs) per 100 000 population and economic losses. All economic indicators are reported in 2021 international dollars (USD) adjusted for purchasing power parity. Joinpoint regression characterized 2000 to 2023 trends. Results From 2000 to 2023, total YLDs increased from 2367.81 (95% uncertainty interval [UI], 1067.67-4969.59) to 2941.68 (95% UI, 1252.99-6816.95) per 100 000 population, while economic losses increased from $80.10 billion (95% UI, $59.60-$104.69 billion) to $363.25 billion (95% UI, $264.04-$502.74 billion). The highest 2023 YLD rate was observed for osteoarthritis and Alzheimer disease and other dementias (369.87 [95% UI, 163.86-752.23] per 100 000 population), whereas the largest 2023 economic loss was observed for osteoarthritis and anxiety disorders ($48.51 billion [95% UI, $31.68-$76.57 billion]). The fastest-growing combination was diabetes, anxiety disorders, and Parkinson disease, with a YLD average annual percentage change (AAPC) of 3.94% (95% CI, 3.79%-4.08%) and an economic loss AAPC of 9.92% (95% CI, 9.69%-10.13%). Conclusions and Relevance In this economic evaluation of the global health and economic burden of multimorbidity among adults aged 60 years or older, multimorbidity burden increased worldwide, with economic losses growing faster than YLDs. Heterogeneity across sex, country income groups, and disease combinations, together with divergence between disability and economic burden, suggest that policy priorities for aging populations should consider both health burden and economic vulnerability.

item.title: Multiple Dimensions of Social Vulnerability and Cervical Cancer Screening Uptake
item.dc:creator: Julie Haury
Jean Baptiste Chanier
Bruno Renevier
Geoffroy Canlorbe
Simon Crequit
item.description:
Authors: Julie Haury, Jean Baptiste Chanier, Bruno Renevier, Geoffroy Canlorbe, Simon Crequit
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639570
Abstract: Importance Despite organized screening programs, persistent social inequalities undermine cervical cancer screening effectiveness in high-income countries, disproportionately affecting the most socially vulnerable women. Objectives To identify distinct social vulnerability profiles among pregnant women and examine their associations with cervical cancer screening adherence and intraepithelial lesion detection. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study assessed all pregnant women 25 years or older who delivered at Centre Hospitalier Intercommunal André-Grégoire, a single tertiary care maternity unit in France, between May 1, 2019, and May 1, 2025. Exposures Social vulnerability was assessed across 15 indicators spanning administrative, psychological, and violence-related domains. Multiple component analysis and hierarchical clustering on principal components identified 6 distinct vulnerability profiles. Multiple logistic regression examined associations between profiles and cervical screening inadequacy (no cervical sample within the last 3 years, including those never screened) and squamous intraepithelial lesion detection, adjusting for maternal age and body mass index. Main Outcomes and Measures Cervical screening inadequacy (primary outcome) and low- and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion detection (secondary outcome). Results Among 18 253 women (median [IQR] age, 32.3 [29.1-36.0] years; median [IQR] body mass index, 25.9 [22.7-29.4]), 10 248 (56.1%) were up to date with screening. Six vulnerability profiles were identified. Compared with the low-vulnerability reference profile, all profiles showed increased odds of screening inadequacy: substance use and psychological vulnerability (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.33; 95% CI, 1.20-1.48), migrant or linguistic barrier (AOR, 3.40; 95% CI, 3.16-3.66), psychological violence (AOR, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.75-2.32), sexual violence (AOR, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.74-2.48), and physical violence (AOR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.19-2.95). Violence-exposed and substance use profiles also had significantly higher proportions of women with a detected intraepithelial lesion despite reduced screening participation. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of pregnant women, distinct social vulnerability profiles were differentially associated with cervical cancer screening inadequacy; women with migration-related barriers experienced the greatest disadvantage, and violence-exposed women showed both reduced screening and elevated disease burden. These findings suggest profile-specific interventions could help reduce cervical cancer screening inequalities among socially vulnerable populations.

item.title: Storage and Disposal of Unused Prescription Opioids for Acute Pain After Emergency Department Discharge
item.dc:creator: Raoul Daoust
David Williamson
Vérilibe Huard
Jeffrey J. Perry
Justin W. Yan
Eddy Lang
Alexis Cournoyer
item.description:
Authors: Raoul Daoust, David Williamson, Vérilibe Huard, Jeffrey J. Perry, Justin W. Yan, Eddy Lang, Alexis Cournoyer, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639607
Abstract: Importance Opioid misuse is a major public health concern, and unused prescription opioids can contribute to this problem. Objective To estimate the proportion of unused opioids among patients discharged from the emergency department (ED) for acute pain, evaluate opioid storage and disposal practices, and identify factors that may motivate patients to return unused opioids. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study, which was a preplanned substudy of a Canadian multicenter prospective cohort study (Quantity of Opioids for Acute Pain and Limit Unused Medication Group [OPUM] study, with recruitment beginning in May 2019 and follow-up ending in January 2024), included consecutive patients aged 18 years or older discharged from the EDs of 7 hospitals in Québec and Ontario with an opioid prescription for an acute pain condition. Participants were followed up at 2 weeks and 3 months. Exposure Opioid prescription for acute pain at ED discharge. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcomes were the proportion of participants with unused opioids at 2 weeks and 3 months after ED discharge, opioid storage practices at 2 weeks, and opioid disposal practices at 3 months. Results Of 2590 enrolled participants in the cohort, 2047 (79.0%) completed the 2-week follow-up and 1835 (70.8%) completed the 3-month follow-up. Among participants who completed the 3-month follow-up, mean (SD) age was 51.3 (15.4) years, 947 (51.6%) were male, and mean pain intensity score at triage was 7.1 (2.3) out of 10. At 2 weeks, 1521 of 1811 participants (84.0%; 95% CI, 82.2%-85.6%) reported unused opioids; 102 of 1525 (6.7%; 95% CI, 5.5%-8.1%) stored their opioids in a locked area and 393 of 1525 (25.8%; 95% CI, 23.6%-28.0%) out of reach of children or teenagers. At 3 months, 926 of 1495 (61.9%; 95% CI, 59.4%-64.4%) reported unused opioids, kept mostly for possible future pain (534 [57.7%; 95% CI, 54.4%-60.9%]) or because participants forgot or lacked time to return them (262 [28.3%; 95% CI, 25.4%-31.3%]). Only 614 of 1835 participants (33.5%; 95% CI, 31.3%-35.7%) indicated they would voluntarily return opioids to the pharmacy if prompted, while 479 (26.1%; 95% CI, 24.1%-28.2%) would not return them regardless of incentive offered. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, 3 months after their ED visit, many participants kept unused prescription opioids at home under suboptimal storage conditions; only one-third were willing to return their opioids to a pharmacy, while more than one-fourth were not. These findings support tailoring opioid prescriptions to individual patient needs to reduce unused medication, alongside strengthening take-back networks and enhancing patient education on safe use, storage, and disposal of opioids.

item.title: Androgen Synthesis Inhibitors vs Androgen Receptor Inhibitors and Survival in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer

Yeonjung Jo
Varun Nandakumar
Zeynep Irem Ozay
Chiara Mercinelli
Gabriel Hooper

item.description:
Authors: Georges Gebrael, Yeonjung Jo, Varun Nandakumar, Zeynep Irem Ozay, Chiara Mercinelli, Gabriel Hooper, Micah Ostrowski, Nicolas Sayegh, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639458
Abstract: Importance In metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), randomized clinical trials directly comparing androgen deprivation therapy intensification using androgen synthesis inhibitors (ASIs) vs next-generation androgen receptor inhibitors (ARIs) are lacking. Objective To compare the outcomes associated with ASI vs ARI intensification therapy among patients with mHSPC in community or academic clinical practices. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a retrospective cohort study of patients diagnosed with mHSPC between February 4, 2013, and April 29, 2024, with follow-up through the July 2024 data cut, providing a median (IQR) follow-up of 25.6 (24.5-26.6) months. Patient-level data were extracted from the nationwide US-based Flatiron Health electronic health record–derived deidentified research database of community and academic practices. Patients with evidence of an mHSPC diagnosis initiating treatment with an ASI (abiraterone acetate) or ARI (apalutamide or enzalutamide) within 3 months prior to or 6 months after an mHSPC diagnosis were eligible. Patients with prior docetaxel receipt were excluded. Exposure Treatment with an ASI vs an ARI. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), defined as time in months from mHSPC diagnosis to death or censoring at last recorded activity. Results Of 3404 patients (median [IQR] age, 73 [66-80] years), 1830 received treatment with an ASI (abiraterone), and 1574 with an ARI (507 apalutamide, 1067 enzalutamide). Following inverse probability of treatment weighting, patients receiving an ARI had significantly longer OS (median, 67.9 months [95% CI, 67.5 months to not reached]) compared with patients treated with the ASI (median, 57.2 months [95% CI, 52.7-63.3 months]) (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.64-0.87]); P &amp;lt; .001). Results were similar in sensitivity analyses using therapy initiation as the index date (HR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.62-0.84]; P &amp;lt; .001) and when restricted to index dates on or after December 16, 2019 (HR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.56-0.81]; P &amp;lt; .001). The association was not modified by insurance status or socioeconomic status. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of 3404 patients with mHSPC, treatment intensification with an ARI was associated with significantly longer OS compared with an ASI. These findings may help guide clinical treatment selection and patient counseling. However, given conflicting clinical practice data across differing database populations, only a randomized clinical trial can definitively answer this question.

item.title: Clinical Evidence on Psilocybin and Its Representation in Media Reporting
item.dc:creator: Kim Madden
Breanne Flood
Imad Kashir
Rayan Ahmad
Hiba Ali
Rotem Petranker
James MacKillop
Anthony Adili
item.description:
Authors: Kim Madden, Breanne Flood, Imad Kashir, Rayan Ahmad, Hiba Ali, Rotem Petranker, James MacKillop, Anthony Adili
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2638843
Abstract: Importance Psilocybin has received increased attention as a potential therapeutic intervention, but it is unclear whether news media reporting reflects the strengths and limitations of the clinical trial evidence. Objective To describe the annual counts of published clinical trials of therapeutic psilocybin and contemporaneous media articles and compare tone, efficacy, and safety messaging. Evidence Review This systematic review included English-language randomized and nonrandomized trials of psilocybin for clinical indications published from January 1, 2014, to October 10, 2024, and media articles describing its clinical use published from January 1, 2014, to April 22, 2025. Trials were found by searching Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and were characterized by design, indication, use of psychotherapy, and reporting of efficacy and safety. Media articles were found through the Factiva database and were characterized by audience, tone, indication, efficacy claim, and safety content. Data were extracted by 2 reviewers. Risk of bias for randomized clinical trials was assessed descriptively using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Findings Annual counts of both published clinical trials (n = 70) and media reports (n = 172) increased from 2018 onward. Depression was the most common clinical indication in trials (47 [67%]) and media articles (138 [80%]), while media articles frequently referenced posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) (74 [43%]) and anxiety (72 [42%]) as clinical indications despite absent and limited trial evidence, respectively, for these conditions. Overall, 49 trials (70%) reported benefit for the primary indication; 125 media articles (73%) made at least 1 positive efficacy claim, and 122 (71%) adopted a favorable tone. Trials typically described small sample sizes of less than 100 participants (65 trials [93%]) and methodologic limitations. Overall, 31 trials (44%) reported safety outcomes, with some (24 [34%]) documenting short-term adverse events, such as transient anxiety, nausea, or headache; long-term safety was rarely assessed (4 trials [6%]). Only 51 media articles (30%) mentioned safety; when harms were discussed, potential long-term psychological risks were sometimes noted (12 articles [7%]). Conclusions and Relevance In this systematic review of clinical trials and media articles, both reported positive effects of therapeutic psilocybin with similar frequency. Academic publications were more cautious and explicit about methodologic limitations, whereas media reports often presented benefits as established, extrapolated them to indications with little or no trial evidence, and provided less safety information. Clarifying these differences in emphasis may support more transparent public communication of indication-specific evidence and uncertainty as interest in psilocybin-assisted treatments grows.

Authors: Zhuo Tony Su, Tyler S. Garman, Carlos A. Rivera Lopez, Ruchika Talwar, Raju Chelluri, Burles A. Johnson, Hiten D. Patel, Akshay Sood, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2640370
Abstract: Importance Although cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy for patients with localized muscle-invasive blader cancer (MIBC) is associated with improved survival, nearly half of these patients are ineligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy and historically proceed to radical cystectomy (RC) without neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Perioperative enfortumab vedotin (EV) plus pembrolizumab with RC is an alternative option, but little is known about its cost-effectiveness compared with surgery alone. Objective To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab for cisplatin-ineligible patients with localized MIBC. Design, Setting, and Participants This economic evaluation developed a decision-analytic Markov model that compared neoadjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab followed by RC and adjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab (intervention arm) vs RC alone (control arm). The sample consisted of simulated patients with MIBC who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The model was informed by efficacy and safety data from the KEYNOTE-905/EV-303 trial, which had a median (range) follow-up of 25.6 (11.8-53.7) months. Analyses were performed between October 2025 and August 2026. Intervention The 2 treatment strategies were (1) neoadjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab followed by RC and adjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab and (2) RC alone. Main Outcomes and Measures Outcomes included life-years, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and direct medical costs estimated from a Medicare payer perspective over a 10-year horizon. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) was assessed against a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per QALY. Scenario, 1-way, and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results The model consisted of 10 000 patients (age at baseline, 73 years; 77 900 males [77.9%]). Over 10 years, adding perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab to treatment was associated with increased projected survival from 4.12 to 5.63 life-years per patient, quality-adjusted survival from 3.20 to 4.51 QALYs per patient, and total costs from $317 513 to $412 160. Higher upfront perioperative therapy costs were partially offset by lower postprogression treatment costs ($12 578 per patient for the intervention arm vs $238 729 per patient for the control arm). Perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab with RC achieved an ICER of $72 460 per QALY vs RC alone and therefore represented a cost-effective treatment approach. In 1-way and scenario sensitivity analyses, the cost-effectiveness result was sensitive to alternative assumptions for key factors, including time horizon length, adjuvant therapy utilization rates, patient age, postprogression treatment mix, drug costs, and health utility before disease progression. In the probabilistic sensitivity analysis, perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab with RC had a 53% probability of being cost-effective vs RC alone at the prespecified willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per QALY. Conclusions and Relevance In this economic evaluation of a simulated cohort of patients with cisplatin-ineligible MIBC, clinical trial–informed modeling suggested that adopting the perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab intervention extends overall survival and quality-adjusted survival and is likely cost-effective in the US.

Authors: Zachariah Thomas, Cindy Y. Jiang, Patrick J. Speck, Emanuele Crupi, Mohammad Jad Moussa, Adrienne Joseph, Carly Stender, Michael Glover, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639517
Abstract: Importance Skin toxic effects are a common early adverse event of enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (EVP) therapy, but its association with clinical outcomes in patients receiving first-line therapy remains uncertain. Objective To evaluate the association between treatment-emergent skin toxic effects and clinical outcomes among patients receiving first-line EVP. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study was performed at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center among adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma receiving first-line EVP therapy between March 3, 2022, and July 31, 2025. Skin toxic effects were used as a time-dependent exposure in Cox proportional hazards regression to account for immortal-time bias. Prespecified sequential adjustment models and 30-day landmark analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. Exposure Treatment-emergent skin toxic effects (rash or pruritus) were identified from medical records. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcome was overall survival (OS). Secondary outcomes included progression-free survival and objective response rate (ORR). OS and PFS were measured from EVP therapy initiation to the respective event or last follow-up. ORR was evaluated among patients with a response assessment after the 30-day landmark, according to skin toxic effects status within the first 30 days. Results Among 185 patients (median age, 73 [IQR, 67-79] years; 140 [75.7%] male), skin toxic effects occurred in 98 (53.0%) at a median of 14 (IQR, 7-28) days after EVP therapy initiation. Skin toxic effects of grade 3 or higher occurred in 10 patients (5.4%). Skin toxic effects resulted in EV dose reduction in 31 patients (16.8%), treatment interruption in 20 (10.8%), and treatment discontinuation in 9 (4.9%). At a median follow-up of 17.7 (IQR, 11.3-24.2) months, Simon-Makuch curves demonstrated longer OS and PFS among all patients and longer OS among patients with visceral metastases in the skin toxic effects stratum than in the no toxicity stratum. In adjusted time-dependent Cox proportional hazards regression, skin toxic effects were associated with longer OS (hazard ratio, 0.34 [95% CI, 0.20-0.57]). The association remained consistent across sequential adjustment models and prespecified 30-day landmark analyses. In the 30-day landmark analyses, associations with PFS and ORR remained directionally favorable but were attenuated after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of 185 patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma receiving first-line EVP therapy, treatment-emergent skin toxic effects were associated with longer OS. These findings support further prospective validation of skin toxic effects as an early clinical marker of treatment benefit and investigation of the biological mechanisms underlying this association.
